transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Chen (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (Aurora Procurement), Aisha Rahman (Aurora Legal), Derek Shaw (CTO), Priya Menon (Security)

Summary: quick procurement kickoff to align on MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approval path, and onboarding timeline. Aisha will lead legal redlines; procurement needs pricing worksheet for executive approval. Customer expressed strong requirements around data residency, encryption/KMS, and breach notificiation windows.

[00:00] Sam: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we appreciate the time. i'm Sam, AE for Redwood, and with me is nina our solution engineer and olivia on CS. we wanted to walk through the MSA/DPA items and the onboarding path so you have what you need for approvals.
[00:20] Marcus: thanks Sam, on our side i'm Marcus from procurement, Aisha is legal, Derek is our CTO, Priya is security. we have a pretty tight timeline, CFO wants vendor approved by end of month if possible.
[00:35] Aisha: hi all. main concerns for us are data residency, deletion at termination, breach notificiation timelines, indemnity and insurance caps. also need to confirm SOC2 and recent pen test.
[00:50] Nina: understood. we can provide our SOC 2 type II report and a pen test summary. for pen test we can share an executive summary and provide contact for the full report under NDA. on data residency we support region pinning and can run the tenancy in your eu-west-1 tenant for the pilot.
[01:10] Derek: quick clarifying q — when you say region pinning, is that hosted or do we need Redwood Private? what's the difference in terms of data transit?
[01:20] Nina: good question. hosted API supports region pinning so the compute and storage can stay in the region, but metadata in control plane may still be in our control plane unless you opt for Private (VPC) deployment. Private gives you customer-managed control plane and can be on-prem or in your VPC — more strict. there are tradeoffs on cost and lead time.
[01:40] Priya: we need to confirm KMS/HSM integration — can we bring our own keys?
[01:45] Sam: yes, BYOK via KMS is supported for Private deployments; for hosted we offer customer key support with managed KMS options. i'll have nina pull the KMS integration note.
[01:55] Marcus: on pricing, procurement needs a clear committed capacity and blowup examples if usage exceeds commit. executive wants the monthly cost and a two-tier for burst capacity.
[02:10] Olivia: we have a standard dedicated/reserved capacity worksheet, and we can give you example unit economics at your expected token rate. we'll include a burst allowance option in the worksheet.
[02:25] Aisha: on the MSA the indemnity clause seems standard but our counsel wants the cap to be X times the fees or a fixed amount; also need a mutual IP clause and data deletion at termination within 30 days.
[02:40] Sam: got it. we usually negotiate indemnity and can share precedent redlines. we'll send a redline with our standard deletions clause and also note the timeline — 30 days is typical but we can discuss.
[02:55] Aisha: also, breach notification window — we need 72 hours. does Redwood commit to that?
[03:05] Nina: we commit to industry-standard notification windows; 72 hours is on the aggressive side but we'll confirm with security. we do have SOC2 controls and PII incident response playbooks.
[03:20] Priya: can you share the playbook and the last pen test date?
[03:25] Nina: yes, last pen test was 2025-11 and we'll include the summary and timeline. full report under NDA.
[03:35] Marcus: procurement path — once legal greenlights the redline, we need pricing approved by finance. can Redwood provide a one-page summary for our CFO?
[03:45] Sam: yes, we'll provide a pricing one-pager with committed/reserved price, burst rates, and an example monthly bill at your projected usage.
[03:55] Derek: performance SLAs — we want 99.9% availability and a latency SLO for p95 under 300ms for text generation. is that realistic on hosted?
[04:10] Nina: for hosted we publish latency profiles from our model catalog; 300ms p95 depends on model and sequence length. for guaranteed SLOs we usually do Dedicated or Private with SLA backing. we can propose a canary and fallback policy too so if capacity is constrained it routes to a compatible variant.
[04:30] Derek: okay, so Dedicated gives SLA and predictability but at higher cost.
[04:35] Sam: correct — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with SLA; Private gives you additional network and compliance controls.
[04:45] Marcus: timeline question — how long for Private deployment onboarding?
[04:50] Nina: Private typically 6-8 weeks to deploy and validate in your VPC, shorter for hosted region pinning (days to a week). for pilots we recommend hosted region pinning first to validate app flows and then move to Private for production.
[05:05] Aisha: for the DPA we need a clause about sub processors and a data flow diagram. can you provide that?
[05:12] Olivia: yes, we'll attach our data flow diagram and a subprocessor list. we update subprocessor list quarterly.
[05:20] Marcus: procurement will need contact for SOC2 attestations and a security contact for any questions.
[05:25] Nina: i'll be the SE contact for technical, and olivia will be account manager. sam will handle pricing and legal coordination.
[05:35] Aisha: on insurance, we typically require $5M cyber liability. is that within your standard?
[05:40] Sam: standard is $3M; we can discuss escalation to $5M but that may require exec approval. we'll flag that in the redline package.
[05:55] Derek: integration question — do you support KV cache persistence and how does that affect log storage and PII?
[06:05] Nina: KV cache is ephemeral by design, we don't persist user prompts beyond retention windows unless caching optimizations are enabled; we'll include details on KV cache behavior and data retention in the security pack.
[06:20] Priya: retention windows — we need ability to set retention to 30 days for logs and delete on demand.
[06:25] Nina: retention controls are configurable with our platform; we'll call out deletion APIs and retention settings in the docs.
[06:35] Marcus: great. can we get a simple onboarding checklist — legal, procurement, security, and technical signoffs?
[06:40] Olivia: yes, we'll send an onboarding checklist with required docs and signoff owners.
[06:48] Sam: suggested next steps: we'll email the redline MSA/DPA and the pricing worksheet by 3/10, SE will send SOC2 and pen test summary by 3/9, and olivia will share onboarding steps and pilot access by 3/8.
[07:05] Aisha: scheduling a legal-only sync for next week would help — i'm available thursday morning.
[07:12] Sam: we'll propose a slot.
[07:15] Marcus: procurement needs the pricing one-pager by friday for CFO review, is that possible?
[07:20] Sam: we'll prioritize and aim for Friday EOD.
[07:30] (cross talk)
[07:40] Derek: on SLA credits — how are they calculated? is it pro-rata or service credit?
[07:45] Nina: we calculate service credits based on monthly uptime percentage and apply credits to future invoices; we'll include the SLA credit table in the MSA.
[07:58] Aisha: also we need to confirm data export formats on termination — do you provide full export of customer data?
[08:05] Olivia: yes, export is available in JSON/ndjson and we'll include the data export guide in the docs.
[08:15] Marcus: any competitors mentioned by our legal — they asked if you have references with other fintechs. can you provide a couple?
[08:22] Sam: yes, we can share anonymized references in finance and healthcare — i'll include two references.
[08:30] Aisha: final question on sub processors — how do we get notified of changes?
[08:35] Nina: we notify customers 30 days before subprocessor changes and publish the list; we'll include language in the DPA.
[08:45] Marcus: ok that's helpful.
[08:55] Sam: quick recap of action items... (recap) sam will send redline MSA/DPA and pricing, nina will send SOC2 and pen test summary, olivia will send onboarding checklist and staging access note, aisha will return legal redlines. we'll schedule legal-only sync and procurement follow-up for pricing approval.
[09:15] Aisha: thanks everyone. let's aim to close redline by next week.
[09:20] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings, "breach notificiation" spelled wrong in transcript, product names sometimes shortened (e.g., Redwood Private -> "Private"), and some speaker attribution is approximate.
